英文: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen! Welcome to Beijing, the capital of the People's Republic of China. My name is your tour guide today. I am very glad to have this opportunity to show you around. If you have any questions, please feel free to ask me at any time.
中文: 各位游客朋友，欢迎来到北京。我是您今天的导游，很高兴带大家游览，有问题随时问我。

英文: Today we are going to visit a famous historic site in Beijing. Before we start, please remember two things: first, please stay with the group; second, no flash photography inside the halls. Now, please follow me and let us begin our wonderful journey.
中文: 今天我们参观北京的一处著名景点。出发前请记住两点：跟紧队伍；殿内不要用闪光灯拍照。现在请跟我来。

英文: Ladies and gentlemen, our tour of today is coming to an end. Thank you for your cooperation and understanding during the trip. I hope you have enjoyed today's visit and gained a deeper understanding of Beijing's history and culture.
中文: 各位游客，今天的游览到此结束。感谢大家的配合与理解，希望大家喜欢今天的行程。

英文: It has been a great pleasure to be your guide today. I sincerely welcome your suggestions for my work. If you have the chance to come to Beijing again, I will be very happy to see you and serve you again. Safe journey home!
中文: 今天能当大家的导游我很荣幸。欢迎对我的工作提出宝贵意见。欢迎再来北京，祝大家一路平安！

英文: Beijing is the capital of China and one of the world's great ancient capitals. It has a history of more than 3,000 years as a city and more than 800 years as a national capital. In 1949, Beijing was chosen as the capital of New China and has since become the political and cultural center of the country.
中文: 北京是中国首都、世界著名古都，建城 3000 余年、建都 800 余年，1949 年成为新中国首都。

英文: Beijing covers an area of about 16,400 square kilometers and has a population of more than 21 million. It administers 16 districts. The city lies in the north of the North China Plain, with mountains on its west, north and northeast sides.
中文: 北京面积约 1.64 万平方公里，常住人口 2100 多万，下辖 16 个区，西、北、东北三面环山。

英文: Beijing has more than 200 scenic spots open to visitors. The city tree is the Chinese scholar tree and the cypress, and the city flowers are the Chinese rose and the chrysanthemum. Beijing is home to eight UNESCO World Heritage Sites, more than any other city in the world.
中文: 北京开放景点 200 多处，市树国槐、侧柏，市花月季、菊花，拥有 8 处世界文化遗产，全球城市之最。

英文: Beijing combines ancient tradition with modern development. In 2008 it hosted the Summer Olympic Games, and in 2022 it became the first city in history to host both the Summer and Winter Olympics. In 2024, the Central Axis of Beijing was added to the World Heritage List.
中文: 北京古今交融：2008 夏奥、2022 冬奥（世界首个双奥之城），2024 年中轴线申遗成功。

英文: Tian'anmen, the Gate of Heavenly Peace, was originally built in 1417 during the Ming Dynasty and was first named Chengtianmen, meaning 'receiving the mandate of heaven.' In 1651 it was rebuilt and renamed Tian'anmen, meaning 'peace under heaven.' It served as the main gate of the Imperial City in the Ming and Qing dynasties.
中文: 天安门原名承天门，建于 1417 年（明永乐十五年），1651 年（清顺治八年）重建改名，意为“受命于天、安邦治民”。

英文: The gate tower stands 34.7 meters high. The tower hall is nine bays wide, and the platform below has five gateways, which together symbolize the supreme status of the feudal emperor. The roof is a double-eaved hip roof covered with golden glazed tiles, the highest grade of Chinese architecture.
中文: 城楼通高 34.7 米，面阔九楹、五个门洞，九五至尊；重檐歇山顶、黄琉璃瓦，最高等级。

英文: In front of the gate flows the Golden Water River, crossed by seven marble bridges. The central bridge, the widest one, was reserved for the emperor and the empress. The bridges on both sides were used by the royal family and officials according to their ranks.
中文: 天安门前金水河上横跨 7 座石桥，中桥最宽，供帝后专用；两侧桥按等级通行王公百官。

英文: Four ornamental columns called huabiao stand in front of and behind the gate, each topped with a mythical beast called hou. The pair inside faces north, urging the emperor to leave the palace and care for his people; the pair outside faces south, watching over his return.
中文: 天安门内外立有 4 根华表，顶端蹲着神兽“犼”：里侧望君出、外侧望君归。

英文: On October 1, 1949, Chairman Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China on the rostrum of Tian'anmen. Since then, Tian'anmen has become the symbol of New China and the venue for major national celebrations and parades.
中文: 1949 年 10 月 1 日开国大典在天安门城楼举行，天安门从此成为新中国象征和重大庆典场所。

英文: Tian'anmen Square covers an area of 440,000 square meters, making it the largest city square in the world. It is surrounded by the Monument to the People's Heroes, the Great Hall of the People, the National Museum of China and the Chairman Mao Memorial Hall.
中文: 天安门广场面积 44 万平方米，世界最大城市广场；四周为人民英雄纪念碑、人民大会堂、国家博物馆、毛主席纪念堂。

英文: The Monument to the People's Heroes stands in the center of the square. It was completed in 1958 and is 37.94 meters high. Chairman Mao wrote the inscription 'Eternal glory to the people's heroes,' and the eight bas-reliefs on the base record major events of modern Chinese history.
中文: 人民英雄纪念碑 1958 年建成、高 37.94 米，毛主席题写“人民英雄永垂不朽”，基座 8 幅浮雕。

英文: The Great Hall of the People stands on the west side of the square. It was built in 1959 in only ten months as one of the Ten Great Buildings of that era. Its auditorium with 10,000 seats is where the National People's Congress holds its sessions.
中文: 人民大会堂位于广场西侧，1959 年十大建筑之一，仅用 10 个月建成，内有万人大会堂。

英文: The National Museum of China is on the east side of the square. Its collections trace Chinese civilization from ancient times to the present. The famous 'Ancient China' permanent display covers more than 5,000 years of Chinese history.
中文: 国家博物馆位于广场东侧，馆藏纵贯中华文明，“古代中国”基本陈列涵盖 5000 多年历史。

英文: The Chairman Mao Memorial Hall was completed in 1977 and stands on the south side of the square. The body of Chairman Mao is preserved there in a crystal coffin, and visitors from all over the country come to pay their respects.
中文: 毛主席纪念堂 1977 年建成，位于广场南侧，毛主席遗体现安放在水晶棺中供瞻仰。

英文: Every day at sunrise and sunset, the national flag is raised and lowered in the square in a solemn ceremony. The flag-raising ceremony has become one of the most popular attractions in Beijing, especially on national holidays.
中文: 每天日出日落举行升降国旗仪式，已成为北京最受欢迎的景观之一，节假日尤为隆重。

英文: In the Ming and Qing dynasties, Tian'anmen was the place where imperial edicts were proclaimed in a ceremony called 'the golden phoenix issuing the edict.' A wooden phoenix holding the imperial decree was lowered from the tower, and officials received it below.
中文: 明清时期天安门举行“金凤颁诏”大典：木雕金凤衔诏书从城楼降下，礼官跪接。

英文: The Forbidden City, now the Palace Museum, was built between 1406 and 1420 under Emperor Yongle of the Ming Dynasty. It served as the imperial palace for 24 emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties for nearly 500 years. In 1987, it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
中文: 故宫 1406-1420 年明永乐年间营建，明清 24 位皇帝在此居住近 500 年，1987 年列入世界遗产。

英文: The Forbidden City covers an area of 720,000 square meters and contains more than 9,000 rooms. It is the largest and best-preserved ancient palace complex in the world. The name comes from the fact that ordinary people were forbidden to enter the palace.
中文: 故宫占地 72 万平方米、房屋 9000 余间，世界现存规模最大、保存最完整的古代宫殿建筑群。

英文: The palace is laid out along a central axis, and the whole complex follows the principle of 'front court, rear residence.' The front part was for state affairs, while the rear part was the living quarters of the emperor and his family.
中文: 故宫沿中轴线布局，前朝后寝：前部处理朝政，后部为帝后生活区。

英文: The Meridian Gate, or Wumen, is the main entrance of the Forbidden City. With its U-shaped plan and five towers, it is also called the Five Phoenix Tower. Important ceremonies took place here, such as the announcement of military victories.
中文: 午门是故宫正门，U 形城台加五座城楼称“五凤楼”，重要典礼如凯旋献俘在此举行。

英文: The Hall of Supreme Harmony, or Taihedian, is the most important building in the palace and the largest existing wooden hall in China, standing 35 meters high. Here the emperor held grand ceremonies such as his enthronement and birthday.
中文: 太和殿是故宫最核心建筑、中国现存最大木结构大殿，高 35 米，皇帝登基、大典在此举行。

英文: Inside the Hall of Supreme Harmony stands the gilded throne, with a plaque above reading 'Be open and aboveboard.' In front of the hall are a bronze tortoise and crane, sundials and measuring vessels, symbolizing longevity and the emperor's authority.
中文: 太和殿内金漆宝座上悬“建极绥猷”匾；殿前陈设铜龟铜鹤、日晷嘉量，象征长寿与皇权。

英文: Behind the Hall of Supreme Harmony are the Hall of Central Harmony and the Hall of Preserving Harmony. The former was where the emperor rested before ceremonies; the latter was used for banquets and later for the final stage of the imperial examination.
中文: 中和殿为皇帝大典前休息处；保和殿用于宴会，清代后期为殿试场所。

英文: Behind the Hall of Preserving Harmony lies a 250-ton marble carving of nine dragons among clouds, the largest stone carving in the Forbidden City. It was transported from a quarry dozens of kilometers away in winter along an ice road.
中文: 保和殿后云龙大石雕重约 250 吨，为故宫最大石雕，冬季泼水成冰道从数十公里外运来。

英文: The Gate of Heavenly Purity leads into the inner court. The Hall of Heavenly Purity was the emperor's bedchamber in the early Qing Dynasty. Above the throne hangs the plaque 'Be open and aboveboard,' behind which the name of the successor was kept secretly.
中文: 乾清门内为后廷；乾清宫是清初皇帝寝宫，正大光明匾后曾藏秘密立储诏书。

英文: The Hall of Union and Peace stands between the Hall of Heavenly Purity and the Hall of Earthly Tranquility. It houses the 25 imperial seals and the plaque 'Wu Wei' written by Emperor Qianlong, meaning 'govern by non-interference.'
中文: 交泰殿位于乾清宫与坤宁宫之间，存放二十五宝，乾隆御笔“无为”匾悬于殿内。

英文: The Hall of Earthly Tranquility was the residence of the empress. In the Qing Dynasty it also served as the wedding chamber for the emperor and empress and as a shamanic shrine of the Manchu royal family.
中文: 坤宁宫为皇后寝宫，清代兼作皇帝大婚洞房，也是满族萨满祭祀场所。

英文: The Hall of Mental Cultivation became the emperor's office and residence from Emperor Yongzheng onward. The famous 'Three Rare Treasures' study of Emperor Qianlong and the screen behind which Empress Dowager Cixi held power are both found here.
中文: 养心殿自雍正起为皇帝理政起居之所，有三希堂和慈禧垂帘听政处。

英文: The Imperial Garden at the north end of the palace is a masterpiece of classical Chinese gardening. Ancient cypresses, rockeries and pavilions create a tranquil landscape within the palace walls. The Gate of Divine Might in the north is the back exit of the palace.
中文: 御花园是古典园林杰作，古柏假山亭台错落；北端神武门是故宫后门。

英文: The Forbidden City is not only a masterpiece of architecture but also a treasure house of culture. The Palace Museum now holds more than 1.8 million cultural relics, many of them national treasures, and receives millions of visitors every year.
中文: 故宫还是文化宝库：馆藏文物 180 余万件，每年接待游客数百万。

英文: The Temple of Heaven was built in 1420 during the reign of Emperor Yongle of the Ming Dynasty. It was first called the Temple of Heaven and Earth, where emperors worshipped both. In 1530, Emperor Jiajing separated the ceremonies and built the Altar of Earth in the north of the city.
中文: 天坛建于 1420 年（明永乐十八年），初名天地坛；1530 年嘉靖帝天地分祀，另建地坛。

英文: The Temple of Heaven covers an area of 2.73 million square meters, about four times the size of the Forbidden City. It is the largest existing ancient sacrificial complex in the world. In 1998, it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
中文: 天坛占地 273 万平方米，约为故宫的 4 倍，世界现存最大祭天建筑群，1998 年列入世界遗产。

英文: The temple was where the emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties worshipped Heaven and prayed for good harvests. In total, 22 emperors held 654 grand ceremonies here. It is a masterpiece of Chinese philosophy, architecture and ritual.
中文: 明清皇帝在此祭天祈谷，22 位皇帝共举行 654 次大典（题库口径），是礼制建筑杰作。

英文: The temple has two main groups of buildings: the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests in the north and the Circular Mound Altar in the south. They are connected by a 360-meter-long raised walkway called the Danbi Bridge, which is higher in the middle than on either side.
中文: 天坛北为祈谷坛（祈年殿）、南为圜丘坛，由 360 米丹陛桥相连，桥面中间高两侧低。

英文: The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests is a circular building 38 meters high, with a triple-eaved roof covered with blue glazed tiles symbolizing Heaven. The hall was built without any interior beams or nails, using only wooden brackets and columns.
中文: 祈年殿高 38 米，三重檐蓝色琉璃瓦象征天；殿内无大梁长檩，全靠斗拱和柱子支撑。

英文: Inside the hall, 28 huge columns support the structure. The four central Dragon Well Pillars represent the four seasons; the twelve inner columns stand for the twelve months, and the twelve outer columns stand for the twelve two-hour periods of the day.
中文: 殿内 28 根大柱：4 根龙井柱代表四季，12 根金柱代表 12 个月，12 根檐柱代表 12 个时辰。

英文: The Circular Mound Altar is a three-tiered white marble platform where the emperor offered sacrifices to Heaven on the winter solstice. Everything here is designed in multiples of nine, the number of the emperor and of Heaven.
中文: 圜丘坛为三层白色石坛，皇帝冬至祭天；坛上处处以九为基数，九为天数、帝王之数。

英文: At the center of the top tier lies the Round Heart Stone. If you stand on it and speak, your voice sounds louder and more resonant. The railings of the altar are all arranged in multiples of nine, reflecting the supreme status of Heaven.
中文: 圜丘上层中心为天心石，站在上面说话声音格外洪亮；栏板数量皆为九的倍数。

英文: The Imperial Vault of Heaven, south of the Hall of Prayer, houses the tablets of Heaven and the imperial ancestors. Its round wall, known as the Echo Wall, carries sound along its surface, and the Three Sound Stones in front return one, two or three echoes.
中文: 皇穹宇供奉昊天上帝牌位，圆形围墙即回音壁，可传声；殿前三音石可闻一至三声回音。

英文: The Echo Wall is one of the four great acoustic buildings of ancient China. Because the wall is perfectly round and smooth, sound waves travel along it and can be heard clearly on the opposite side, a wonder of ancient acoustics.
中文: 回音壁是中国古代四大声学建筑之一，墙壁光滑圆形，声波沿壁传播，对面清晰可闻。

英文: The Seven Star Stones in the east of the altar area represent the seven mountains where ancient emperors made sacrifices. A small hill was added later, and together they symbolize the worship of mountains in the traditional ritual system.
中文: 七星石象征古代帝王祭祀的七座名山，清代增置一小石象征泰山，寓意江山一统。

英文: The Hall of Abstinence was where the emperor fasted before the ceremony. In the Qing Dynasty, the emperor also held the Grand Prayer Ceremony at the Hall of Prayer in the first month of the lunar year to pray for a good harvest.
中文: 斋宫是皇帝祭前斋戒之所；清代每年正月在祈年殿举行祈谷大典，祈求五谷丰登。

英文: The Summer Palace, known as Yiheyuan, is the best-preserved imperial garden in China. It was first built in 1750 as the Garden of Clear Ripples for Emperor Qianlong's mother. In 1860 it was destroyed by the Anglo-French forces, and in 1888 Empress Dowager Cixi rebuilt it with funds intended for the navy.
中文: 颐和园前身清漪园 1750 年始建；1860 年被英法联军焚毁，1888 年慈禧挪用海军经费重建并改名。

英文: In 1998, the Summer Palace was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The garden covers an area of 290 hectares, about three quarters of which is water. It is a masterpiece of Chinese landscape garden design.
中文: 颐和园 1998 年列入世界遗产，占地 290 公顷，约四分之三为水面，中国古典园林杰作。

英文: The garden is divided into the court area, the Longevity Hill area and the Kunming Lake area. The design follows the principle of 'borrowing scenery': the lake reflects the hill, and the distant mountains frame the view.
中文: 全园分宫廷区、万寿山前山景区、昆明湖景区；借景手法：湖映山、远山入画。

英文: The East Palace Gate is the main entrance of the garden. Behind it stands the Hall of Benevolence and Longevity, where Empress Dowager Cixi and Emperor Guangxu handled state affairs. The hall is named after a saying that benevolent rulers enjoy long life.
中文: 东宫门入园；仁寿殿是慈禧、光绪处理政务之所，殿名取“仁者寿”之意。

英文: The Hall of Jade Ripples was the residence of Emperor Guangxu. After the failure of the Hundred Days' Reform in 1898, Cixi put him under house arrest here for ten years, and the story is still told by the walls of the courtyard.
中文: 玉澜堂为光绪寝宫；1898 年戊戌变法失败后，慈禧在此囚禁光绪达十年。

英文: The Hall of Happiness and Longevity was the private residence of Empress Dowager Cixi. The courtyard is famous for its huge bronze vase and an ancient wisteria more than two hundred years old.
中文: 乐寿堂是慈禧的寝宫，院内有铜铸“太平缸”（寓意太平）和 200 多年的紫藤。

英文: The Long Corridor is 728 meters long with 273 sections, decorated with more than 14,000 colorful paintings of landscapes, flowers and stories from classical literature. It is listed in the Guinness Book of World Records as the longest corridor in the world.
中文: 长廊长 728 米、273 间，彩画 14000 余幅，1992 年列入吉尼斯世界纪录，世界最长画廊。

英文: In the center of the front of Longevity Hill stands the Tower of Buddhist Incense, a 41-meter-high octagonal pavilion with three stories and four eaves. It is the symbol of the Summer Palace and the highest building in the garden.
中文: 万寿山前山中轴线上矗立佛香阁，高 41 米，八面三层四重檐，是颐和园标志性建筑。

英文: Below the Tower of Buddhist Incense is the Hall of Dispelling Clouds, the most magnificent hall in the garden, where Cixi celebrated her birthdays. The layout of this building group is modeled on the imperial palace in miniature.
中文: 佛香阁下为排云殿，全园最壮丽的殿堂，慈禧在此庆寿；建筑群仿皇宫格局缩小而成。

英文: The Kunming Lake covers about 220 hectares. The Seventeen-Arch Bridge connects the east bank with South Lake Island. The bridge is 150 meters long, and its arches are designed with the number nine in mind, the emperor's number.
中文: 昆明湖水面约 220 公顷；十七孔桥长 150 米，连接东岸与南湖岛，桥孔取九之倍数。

英文: On the east shore of the lake stands a bronze ox, cast in 1755, with an inscription saying it was made to suppress floods. According to legend, the ox is the guardian of the waters of Kunming Lake.
中文: 昆明湖东岸有 1755 年铸造的铜牛，身上铸铭文，寓意镇水，守护昆明湖。

英文: The Marble Boat, also called the Boat of Purity and Ease, is a 36-meter-long stone boat at the west end of the Long Corridor. Cixi liked to enjoy tea here in summer, and its elegant upper pavilion was added in 1893.
中文: 长廊西端石舫（清晏舫）长 36 米，慈禧常在此品茗赏景，1893 年增建西式舱楼。

英文: The Great Wall is the largest military defense project in ancient China and a symbol of the Chinese nation. The building of walls began in the 7th century BC, and the separate walls were first connected during the Qin Dynasty under Emperor Qin Shi Huang.
中文: 长城是中国古代最宏大的军事防御工程，始建于公元前 7 世纪，秦始皇首筑万里长城。

英文: In 1987, the Great Wall was among the first sites in China to be inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. In 2012, the total length of the walls of all dynasties was measured at 21,196 kilometers.
中文: 1987 年长城列入世界遗产（中国首批）；2012 年测得历代长城总长 21196.18 公里。

英文: The most famous section of the Great Wall near Beijing is Badaling, about 70 kilometers northwest of the city center. It was a key pass on the route to the north, and its name means 'a place leading in all directions.'
中文: 八达岭长城位于北京西北约 70 公里，是通往塞外的咽喉要道，“八达”意为四通八达。

英文: The wall at Badaling was built in the Ming Dynasty with rammed earth at the core and bricks and stone on the surface. It is about 7.8 meters high on average and wide enough for five horses or ten soldiers to march side by side.
中文: 八达岭长城为明代所建，内填夯土外包砖石，平均高 7.8 米，可容五马并骑、十人并进。

英文: Watchtowers were built along the wall at intervals. Soldiers used them to keep watch, to store weapons, and to send signals with smoke by day and fire by night. Beacon towers were the 'telephone system' of ancient China.
中文: 城墙上间隔建有敌台，用于瞭望、存放武器；烽火台白天燃烟、夜间举火传递军情。

英文: The wall follows the ridges of the mountains, rising and falling with the terrain. It was always built on the highest and most dangerous points, which made it extremely difficult for invaders to approach.
中文: 长城沿山脊起伏修筑，总是建在最高最险处，使来犯之敌难以接近。

英文: Badaling lies in the Juyongguan Pass area, one of the most important passes of the Great Wall. The pass guarded the road from Beijing to the grasslands of Inner Mongolia and was the site of many famous battles.
中文: 八达岭位于居庸关（关沟）一带，居庸关是长城重要关隘，扼守北京通往内蒙古草原的孔道。

英文: The highest point of the tourist area at Badaling is the North Eighth Watchtower, about 888 meters above sea level. From there, visitors can see the wall winding over the mountains like a giant dragon.
中文: 八达岭游览区最高点为北八楼，海拔约 888 米，登临可望长城如巨龙蜿蜒于群山之巅。

英文: Chairman Mao once wrote in a poem: 'He who has never been to the Great Wall is not a true man.' Because of this famous line, climbing to the top of the wall has become a must-do for visitors from all over the world.
中文: 毛泽东词句“不到长城非好汉”使登长城成为中外游客的必选项目。

英文: The Great Wall is not only a great military work but also a wonder of human civilization. It reflects the wisdom, hard work and determination of the Chinese people, and it is the pride of every Chinese person.
中文: 长城不仅是军事工程，更是人类文明奇迹，凝聚中华民族的智慧与毅力，是每个中国人的骄傲。

英文: The Ming Tombs are the imperial tombs of 13 of the 16 emperors of the Ming Dynasty, located at the foot of Tianshou Mountain, about 50 kilometers north of Beijing. The first tomb was built in 1409, and construction continued for more than 200 years.
中文: 明十三陵是明朝 13 位皇帝的陵墓群，位于北京以北天寿山麓，1409 年始建，持续 200 余年。

英文: The tombs cover an area of about 40 square kilometers. In 2003, they were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties.
中文: 十三陵占地约 40 平方公里，2003 年作为“明清皇家陵寝”扩展项目列入世界遗产。

英文: The emperors buried here range from Emperor Yongle to Emperor Chongzhen. Three Ming emperors are not buried here: the founder Zhu Yuanzhang lies in Nanjing, and Emperor Jianwen and Emperor Jingtai died or were removed from the throne in special circumstances.
中文: 从永乐到崇祯共 13 帝葬此；太祖朱元璋葬南京、建文帝失踪、景泰帝被废葬金山，未入陵区。

英文: A seven-kilometer-long Sacred Way leads to the tombs, lined with 36 large stone statues: twelve pairs of stone animals and six pairs of stone officials. They guard the road and show the power and dignity of the emperors.
中文: 神道长 7 公里，两侧排列石象生 36 尊：石兽 12 对、石人 6 对，显示帝王威仪。

英文: The largest and most important tomb is Changling, the tomb of Emperor Yongle, the third emperor of the Ming Dynasty. Its construction began in 1409, and the emperor was buried here in 1424.
中文: 规模最大的是长陵，明成祖朱棣之陵，1409 年始建，1424 年葬入。

英文: The main hall of Changling, the Hall of Eminent Favor, is one of the largest wooden halls in China. Its 60 huge pillars are made of precious nanmu wood, and the pillars were left unpainted to show the beauty of the wood.
中文: 长陵祾恩殿是中国现存最大的楠木殿之一，60 根金丝楠木大柱不施彩绘，尽显木纹之美。

英文: The only tomb that has been excavated is Dingling, the tomb of Emperor Wanli. In 1956, archaeologists opened its underground palace, which lies about 27 meters below the surface and was built entirely of stone without a single beam.
中文: 唯一被发掘的是定陵（万历帝），1956 年考古发掘，地下宫殿距地表约 27 米，全石结构无梁。

英文: The underground palace of Dingling has five chambers. It yielded more than 3,000 cultural relics, including the golden crown of Emperor Wanli and the phoenix crowns of his two empresses.
中文: 定陵地宫有 5 个殿堂，出土文物 3000 余件，包括万历帝金冠和两位皇后的凤冠。

英文: The excavation of Dingling was a milestone in Chinese archaeology, but the changes in temperature and humidity damaged some relics. The experience led China to stop excavating imperial tombs for many years afterwards.
中文: 定陵发掘是中国考古里程碑，但因温湿度变化文物受损，此后中国多年不再发掘帝陵。

英文: The site was chosen strictly according to fengshui: Tianshou Mountain faces south, with mountains behind it and a river in front, a position believed to be perfect for the eternal rest of the emperors.
中文: 陵址严格按风水选址：天寿山坐北朝南、背山面水，被视为理想的万年吉壤。

英文: Each tomb once had its own above-ground palace complex, including a Soul Tower and a sacrificial hall, all enclosed by a red wall. Most of the wooden buildings were burned or destroyed over the centuries.
中文: 每座陵原有地上建筑群：明楼、祾恩殿等，红墙环绕；木构建筑大多毁于历代战火。

英文: Today the Ming Tombs are a popular scenic area and a lesson in history. Visitors can learn about the rise and fall of the Ming Dynasty while walking among the ancient tombs, cypresses and stone carvings.
中文: 今天的十三陵是著名景区，也是历史课堂：漫步古陵、古柏与石雕之间，读懂明朝兴衰。

英文: The Zhoukoudian Peking Man Site, about 50 kilometers southwest of Beijing, is one of the most important archaeological sites in the world. In 1929, the first skull of Peking Man, who lived about 700,000 years ago, was discovered here.
中文: 周口店北京人遗址位于北京西南约 50 公里，1929 年发现第一个北京人头盖骨，距今约 70 万年。

英文: In 1987, the Zhoukoudian site was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The discoveries proved that Peking Man used fire and made stone tools, making the site a key link in the study of human evolution.
中文: 1987 年周口店列入世界遗产；发现证明北京人会用火、会打制石器，是研究人类进化的重要环节。

英文: The Grand Canal is the longest man-made canal in the world, running about 1,794 kilometers from Beijing in the north to Hangzhou in the south. It was first built in the 5th century BC and fully connected during the Sui Dynasty.
中文: 京杭大运河全长约 1794 公里，北起北京南至杭州，始凿于公元前 5 世纪，隋代全线贯通。

英文: In 2014, the Grand Canal was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Its northern starting point lies in Beijing, and the city preserves many canal-related sites along the route.
中文: 2014 年大运河列入世界遗产；大运河北端起点在北京，沿线保留众多相关遗产点。

英文: The Central Axis of Beijing is a 7.8-kilometer-long line running through the center of the city, from the Bell and Drum Towers in the north to Yongding Gate in the south. It is the backbone of the layout of old Beijing.
中文: 北京中轴线南北长 7.8 公里，北起钟鼓楼、南至永定门，是古都北京城市布局的脊梁。

英文: On July 27, 2024, the Central Axis of Beijing was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. It is regarded as the best-preserved example of the planning principles of an ancient Chinese capital.
中文: 2024 年 7 月 27 日北京中轴线申遗成功，被视为中国古代都城规划理念保存最完好的范例。

英文: Prince Gong's Mansion is the largest and best-preserved prince's mansion in Beijing, covering about 60,000 square meters. It was first built for Heshen, a powerful official of the Qianlong period, and later became the residence of Prince Gong.
中文: 恭王府是北京现存规模最大、保存最完整的王府，占地约 6 万平方米，初为和珅宅邸，后为恭亲王奕訢府。

英文: The mansion is famous for its garden, called the Cui Jin Garden, which blends the garden styles of northern and southern China. The whole complex follows the Qing Dynasty mansion pattern of 'residence in front, garden at the back.'
中文: 恭王府花园萃锦园融合南北园林风格，整体遵循清代王府“前宅后园”格局。

英文: Beihai Park, west of the Forbidden City, is one of the oldest and best-preserved imperial gardens in China, with a history of more than 800 years. The park centers on the White Dagoba, a Tibetan-style stupa on Qionghua Island.
中文: 北海公园位于故宫西侧，有 800 多年历史；琼华岛上的白塔是藏式佛塔，为公园标志。

英文: The White Dagoba was built in 1651 to celebrate the visit of the Fifth Dalai Lama to Beijing. The park's lake is said to have been modeled on the fairy mountains of Chinese mythology.
中文: 白塔建于 1651 年，为纪念五世达赖喇嘛进京而建；太液池仿神话中“一池三山”布局。

英文: Jingshan Park is a hill park just north of the Forbidden City. The hill was formed from the earth dug out to create the moat of the Forbidden City. From the top, visitors enjoy a panoramic view of the whole palace.
中文: 景山位于故宫北侧，由挖护城河的泥土堆成；登顶可俯瞰故宫全景。

英文: The hill is also called Coal Hill. At its eastern foot, the last Ming emperor, Chongzhen, hanged himself in 1644 when the rebels entered Beijing, which marked the end of the Ming Dynasty.
中文: 景山又称煤山；1644 年李自成进城时，崇祯帝在山东麓自缢，明朝灭亡。

英文: The Lama Temple, or Yonghegong, is the largest and best-preserved lama temple in Beijing. It was originally the residence of Prince Yongzheng before he became emperor, and it was converted into a lamasery in 1744.
中文: 雍和宫是北京规模最大、保存最完整的藏传佛教寺院，原为雍正帝潜邸，1744 年改为喇嘛庙。

英文: The temple is famous for the 18-meter-high statue of Maitreya Buddha, carved from a single piece of white sandalwood. The hall that houses it is the tallest building in the temple.
中文: 雍和宫万福阁内 18 米高的弥勒佛由整根白檀木雕成，为宫内最高建筑。

英文: The Olympic Park is located at the north end of the Central Axis of Beijing. It was the main venue area of the 2008 Beijing Olympic Games and also hosted events of the 2022 Winter Olympics.
中文: 奥林匹克公园位于北京中轴线北端，是 2008 年奥运会主会场区，2022 年冬奥会也在此办赛。

英文: The most famous buildings in the park are the National Stadium, called the Bird's Nest for its steel structure, and the National Aquatics Center, called the Water Cube. Both have become landmarks of modern Beijing.
中文: 园内最著名建筑是“鸟巢”国家体育场和“水立方”国家游泳中心，已成为北京新地标。

英文: The Confucius Temple in Beijing, built in 1302, is the second largest Confucius temple in China. The stone tablets in its courtyard record the names of successful candidates of the imperial examinations.
中文: 北京孔庙始建于 1302 年，中国第二大孔庙；院内石碑记录历代进士题名。

英文: Next to the temple is the Imperial College, or Guozijian, the highest educational institution of the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties. Its center is the Biyong Hall, surrounded by a square pool of water.
中文: 国子监是元明清三朝最高学府，与孔庙相邻；中心辟雍殿四面环水。

英文: Beijing has eight UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Great Wall, the Forbidden City, the Zhoukoudian Peking Man Site, the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace, the Ming Tombs, the Grand Canal and the Central Axis.
中文: 北京现有 8 处世界遗产：长城、故宫、周口店、天坛、颐和园、明十三陵、大运河、中轴线。

英文: Beijing has many intangible cultural heritage items, such as Peking Opera, which combines singing, acting and acrobatics, and the traditional craft of cloisonné, called Jingtailan, famous for its blue enamel patterns.
中文: 北京非遗丰富：京剧集唱念做打于一身；景泰蓝（铜胎掐丝珐琅）以蓝色釉料闻名。

英文: Beijing has more than 200 museums, including the Palace Museum, the National Museum of China and the Capital Museum. The city is working to become a 'city of museums,' with a museum in every district.
中文: 北京有 200 多座博物馆，包括故宫博物院、国家博物馆、首都博物馆，正在建设“博物馆之城”。

英文: Beijing is rich in red tourism resources. Sites such as Tian'anmen Square and the memorial halls of revolutionary leaders are important places for patriotic education and for learning the history of the Communist Party of China.
中文: 北京红色资源丰富：天安门广场、革命领袖纪念场馆等是开展爱国主义教育的重要场所。

英文: Hutongs and siheyuan, the traditional courtyard houses of Beijing, form a living museum of old Beijing life. The hutong system was formed in the Yuan Dynasty, and the best-preserved areas are around Shichahai and Nanluoguxiang.
中文: 胡同与四合院是老北京生活的活化石，胡同格局始于元代，保存最好的是什刹海、南锣鼓巷一带。

英文: Beijing's famous commercial streets include Wangfujing, the most prosperous shopping street, Qianmen, the traditional commercial area, and Liulichang, the street of antiques and calligraphy. Its time-honored brands include Quanjude Roast Duck and Tongrentang Chinese Medicine, both with histories of more than a hundred years.
中文: 北京著名商业街有王府井（最繁华）、前门（传统商业区）、琉璃厂（古玩书画街）；老字号有全聚德烤鸭、同仁堂中药，均有百年以上历史。

英文: The Beijing Tourism Regulations came into force on August 1, 2017. They are the local regulations that govern tourism in Beijing, covering tourism planning, market order and the protection of tourists' rights.
中文: 《北京市旅游条例》2017 年 8 月 1 日起施行，是规范北京旅游的地方性法规，涵盖规划、市场秩序、游客权益等。

英文: The regulations pay special attention to the 'one-day tour' market. Travel agencies and guides must provide services according to the contract, and forced shopping and the use of unqualified vehicles are strictly prohibited.
中文: 条例重点规范“一日游”市场：旅行社和导游须按合同履约，严禁强制购物、使用非法车辆。

英文: Under the regulations, tour guides must carry their licenses and follow professional standards. The regulations also encourage civilized tourism and require tourists to respect local customs and protect cultural relics.
中文: 条例要求导游持证上岗、规范服务；倡导文明旅游，游客应尊重风俗、爱护文物。

英文: Beijing is the capital of China and a famous historical and cultural city with a history of more than 3,000 years as a city and over 800 years as a national capital.
中文: 北京是中国的首都，是一座有着三千多年建城史和八百多年建都史的历史文化名城。

英文: The Forbidden City, known as Zijincheng in Chinese, was the imperial palace of the Ming and Qing dynasties. It is the largest and best-preserved ancient palace complex in the world.
中文: 故宫旧称紫禁城，是明清两代的皇宫，也是世界上现存规模最大、保存最完整的古代宫殿建筑群。

英文: The Great Wall is a symbol of the Chinese nation and a wonder of human civilization. In 1987, it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as one of the first Chinese sites.
中文: 长城是中华民族的象征，是人类文明的奇迹，1987 年被联合国教科文组织列入《世界遗产名录》。

英文: As a tour guide, my duty is to provide considerate and enthusiastic service to the tourists and to make sure that everyone has a safe and enjoyable trip. I will do my best to answer your questions and to make your stay in Beijing a pleasant memory.
中文: 作为一名导游，我的职责是为游客提供周到、热情的服务，并确保大家旅途安全愉快；我会尽力解答问题，让北京之行成为美好回忆。

英文: The Summer Palace is a masterpiece of Chinese landscape garden design, integrating natural scenery with man-made structures in perfect harmony. The garden was opened to the public as a park in 1914 and has become one of the most popular tourist attractions in Beijing.
中文: 颐和园是中国园林设计艺术的杰作，它将自然景观与人工建筑完美和谐地融为一体；1914 年作为公园开放，现为北京最受欢迎的景区之一。

英文: Please keep your ticket with you and follow the guide closely. The group will gather here at four o'clock sharp this afternoon. If you get separated from the group, please stay where you are and call the number on your name card.
中文: 请保管好您的门票并紧跟导游。请大家今天下午四点整在这里集合。如果走散，请在原地等候并拨打胸卡上的电话。

英文: Ladies and gentlemen, we are now arriving at the Badaling section of the Great Wall. You will have two hours to explore, and we will meet at the parking lot.
中文: 各位游客，我们现在即将到达八达岭长城段。大家将有两个小时的游览时间，我们将在停车场集合。

英文: In case of emergency, please contact the tour leader or dial the local emergency number. Your safety is our first priority. Please also take good care of your personal belongings, especially your passport and wallet, during the whole trip.
中文: 如遇紧急情况，请联系领队或拨打当地紧急电话。您的安全是我们的第一要务；请全程保管好随身物品，尤其是护照和钱包。

英文: When receiving a group at the airport, the local guide should arrive 30 minutes before the scheduled time, hold a sign with the group name, and check the flight arrival information in advance.
中文: 接站服务：提前 30 分钟到达，举接站牌，事先核实航班到达信息。

英文: Before the tour, the guide should make a plan, prepare the necessary documents and materials, and check the weather and traffic conditions. Good preparation is the key to a successful tour.
中文: 出发前准备：制定计划、备齐证件资料、了解天气路况；准备充分是成功游览的关键。

英文: During the tour, if a tourist gets lost, the guide should first calm the whole group, then contact the local police and the tourist's companions. The guide should retrace the route, check the meeting points, and wait at the hotel if the tourist returns by himself.
中文: 游览中游客走失：先安抚全团，再联系景区工作人员、警方和同伴；沿原路寻找、到集合点查找，游客自行返回时在饭店等候。

英文: If a tourist falls ill, the guide should give first aid if possible, help the tourist see a doctor, and arrange for someone to accompany him. The guide should also inform the travel agency and keep a record.
中文: 游客患病：尽量施救，协助就医并安排陪同，同时报告旅行社并做好记录。

英文: If a tourist asks to change the itinerary, the guide should explain that the schedule is fixed by the contract, and only the group leader can discuss changes with the travel agency.
中文: 游客要求变更行程：说明行程按合同执行，只能由领队与旅行社协商调整。

英文: When seeing off the group, the guide should check the luggage, remind the tourists of the departure time and the documents they need, and thank them for their cooperation during the trip.
中文: 送站服务：清点行李、提醒出发时间和所需证件，感谢游客一路配合。

英文: In 2024, the Central Axis of Beijing was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on July 27. This 7.8-kilometer axis is the backbone of the old city's layout and represents the highest achievement of ancient Chinese capital planning.
中文: 2024 年 7 月 27 日，北京中轴线申遗成功（联合国教科文组织世界遗产），这条 7.8 公里的轴线是古都布局的脊梁，代表中国古代都城规划最高成就。

英文: In 2024, Beijing continued to develop as an international exchange center, hosting major events such as the China International Fair for Trade in Services and the Zhongguancun Forum. These events strengthened Beijing's role on the world stage.
中文: 2024 年北京持续建设国际交往中心，成功举办中国国际服务贸易交易会（服贸会）和中关村论坛等重大活动，进一步提升了国际影响力。

英文: In the first half of 2025, Beijing made new progress in ecological conservation. The city's forest coverage rate increased and air quality continued to improve. Beijing is becoming a greener and more livable city.
中文: 2025 年上半年，北京在生态保护方面取得新进展：森林覆盖率提升、空气质量持续改善，北京正成为更绿色更宜居的城市。

英文: New cultural and tourism policies were implemented in Beijing in 2025, including measures to promote digital cultural experiences and smart tourism. The city encourages the integration of culture, technology and tourism.
中文: 2025 年北京实施新的文旅政策，推动数字文化体验和智慧旅游发展，鼓励文化、科技与旅游深度融合。
